body:
### What happened?

hi
running  on self-hosted runners actions/download-artifact@v4 i get this error
**Starting download of artifact to: /xxxx/xxxx
(node:137) [DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated due to security and usability issues. Please use the Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe(), or Buffer.from() methods instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)**

iv checked the  actions/upload-artifact@v4 action which does not have this error and seems actions/github node package needs to be upgraded to 6.x.x.

https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/package.json#L34 has 6..0.0 and https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/main/package.json#L33 has 5.1.1.

reference of simular issue: https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/1618

regards 


### What did you expect to happen?

no DeprecationWarning: Buffer() error or simular, action should run smoothly

### How can we reproduce it?

any usage of actions/download-artifact@v4 

### Anything else we need to know?

be happy to raise pr if it helps

### What version of the action are you using?

4 (latest)

### What are your runner environments?

linux, self-hosted

### Are you on GitHub Enterprise Server? If so, what version?

GHEC

comments.body: Same issue happened to me right now: https://github.com/umccr/gatk-bwamem-jni/actions/runs/13716508594/job/38362482726#step:7:34

@brainstorm yes its been happening for sometime now, it happens on every call to the download action as far as i can see. it just needs  actions/github to be bumped upto  v6.x.x. like the upload action has,

Using the suggestion from Github I traced the problem myself in my Github actions using:

```
      - name: Download code coverage results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4.2.1
        env:
          NODE_OPTIONS: "--trace-deprecation"
```

Here is what I got. Using even the latest version of download-artifact@v.4.2.1 released 2 days ago.

I traced the buffer issue here:

```
Starting download of artifact to: /home/runner/work/REDACTED/REDACTED/coverage
21(node:1595) [DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated due to security and usability issues. Please use the Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe(), or Buffer.from() methods instead.
22 at showFlaggedDeprecation (node:buffer:189:11)
23 at new Buffer (node:buffer:267:3)
24 at new UnzipStream (/home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:110127:17)
25 at new Extract (/home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:109833:24)
26 at Object.Extract (/home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:109828:12)
27 at /home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:2240:46
28 at new Promise (<anonymous>)
29 at /home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:2221:16
30 at Generator.next (<anonymous>)
31 at fulfilled (/home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:2150:58)
```

The issue is clearly coming from the GitHub Actions download-artifact action itself (v4.2.1), specifically in the unzipping functionality. The deprecated `Buffer()` constructor is being used in the `UnzipStream` class within the action's code.

This should be updated immediately and from looking around, it seems to be a potentially severe bug.

The deprecation notice for Node [DEP0005](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/deprecations.html#DEP0005) also appears in the logs from this repo's own [.github/workflows/test.yml](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml) workflow, for instance:

https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/actions/runs/13950097417/job/39047065551

=> Download all Artifacts

https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/actions/runs/13950097417/job/39047065551#step:15:359

> (node:2087) [DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated due to security and usability issues. Please use the Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe(), or Buffer.from() methods instead.

From the debug logs of @825i:

> 24 at new UnzipStream (/home/runner/work/_actions/actions/download-artifact/v4.2.1/dist/index.js:110127:17)

The [dist](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/tree/main/dist) directory is built by `ncc` from the source code of this repo and its `dependencies`.

`UnzipStream` comes from `function UnzipStream(options)` which is sourced from https://github.com/mhr3/unzip-stream/blob/4a4be03d5e13ce5408b8be3dee970d15212ca532/lib/unzip-stream.js#L39-L52

```text
$ npm ls unzip-stream
download-artifact@4.2.0
└─┬ @actions/artifact@2.3.2
  └── unzip-stream@0.3.1
```

[@actions/artifact@2.3.2](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/main/packages/artifact/RELEASES.md) is the `latest` release

[unzip-stream@0.3.4](https://github.com/mhr3/unzip-stream/releases/tag/v0.3.4) (`latest`) also uses the deprecated Buffer()
> `this.data = new Buffer('');`

so it seems there is no simple solution to removing the Node [DEP0005](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/deprecations.html#DEP0005) deprecation.

Also note that the deprecation warning is only output because this is a JavaScript Action and not an npm module, otherwise it would be suppressed to avoid end-users seeing the warning:

[DEP0005](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/deprecations.html#DEP0005) says:

> Without --pending-deprecation, runtime warnings occur only for code not in node_modules. This means there will not be deprecation warnings for Buffer() usage in dependencies. With --pending-deprecation, a runtime warning results no matter where the Buffer() usage occurs.

The deprecation warning can be reproduced in https://github.com/actions/toolkit/tree/main/packages/artifact with `npm test` if options are set:

```shell
export NODE_OPTIONS="--pending-deprecation --trace-deprecation"
```
Thanks really for such thorough investigating Mike. At least in our case we'll just tag it and bag it as something we can't fix.

- I have opened https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2003 to list it where the problem originates from. I don't know whether this can be addressed or not. There are many other deprecations in that repo.

This still reproduces with `actions/download-artifact@v8.0.1`.

I checked the current `v8.0.1` tag locally:

```text
actions/download-artifact@v8.0.1
commit: 3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c
action.yml: runs.using: node24
package.json: @actions/artifact ^6.2.1
package-lock.json: @actions/artifact 6.2.1 -> unzip-stream ^0.3.1
package-lock.json: unzip-stream 0.3.4
```

The bundled `dist/index.js` for `v8.0.1` still contains the deprecated constructor in the unzip path, for example:

```text
dist/index.js:67532    this.data = new Buffer('');
dist/index.js:67720    this.data = new Buffer('');
dist/index.js:68338    this.data = new Buffer('');
dist/index.js:68351    this.data = new Buffer('');
```

Those lines are in the bundled `unzip-stream` implementation used by the `@actions/artifact` download/decompress path.

I also saw the warning in a workflow using `actions/download-artifact@v8`:

```text
Run actions/download-artifact@v8
Downloading single artifact
Starting download of artifact to: /home/runner/work/_temp/open-code-review-output
(node:2158) [DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated due to security and usability issues. Please use the Buffer.alloc(), Buffer.allocUnsafe(), or Buffer.from() methods instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
SHA256 digest of downloaded artifact is ...
Artifact download completed successfully.
```

So the action has moved to Node 24, but the warning remains because the packaged download/decompression dependency still contains `new Buffer(...)`.

It looks like the fix probably needs to happen in `@actions/artifact` by replacing or patching the `unzip-stream` dependency, then rebuilding this action's `dist`. I realize actions/toolkit#2003 tracks the toolkit side; adding this note here because the issue is still visible to `download-artifact@v8` users.

Follow-up: I checked whether a fix PR already exists at the source dependency. There are already open PRs in `mhr3/unzip-stream` that replace deprecated `Buffer` constructor calls:

- https://github.com/mhr3/unzip-stream/pull/51
- https://github.com/mhr3/unzip-stream/pull/49

I also tried the obvious `@actions/artifact` replacement path locally. Swapping to `unzipper` changed the existing malicious archive/path traversal regression behavior, and other extractor options such as `extract-zip` still introduce transitive runtime `new Buffer(...)` usage through ZIP reader dependencies. So the least risky fix path appears to be:

1. Merge/release the `unzip-stream` `Buffer.from`/`Buffer.alloc` fix.
2. Update `@actions/artifact` to consume the patched `unzip-stream` release.
3. Rebuild/release `actions/download-artifact` so the bundled `dist` no longer contains the deprecated constructor.
`unzip-stream` appears to be unmaintained: no new commits in over 2 years and no issues closed in nearly 5 years.

> `unzip-stream` appears to be unmaintained: no new commits in over 2 years and no issues closed in nearly 5 years.

We have completely replaced this with a small composite action:

```
# .github/actions/download-artifact-gh/action.yml
name: Download artifact (gh)
description: Download a workflow artifact via gh CLI, no unzip-stream / Buffer() warning
inputs:
  name:        { description: Artifact name, required: true }
  path:        { description: Destination dir, default: "." }
  run-id:      { description: Run ID, default: "${{ github.run_id }}" }
  repo:        { description: owner/repo, default: "${{ github.repository }}" }
  github-token:{ default: "${{ github.token }}" }
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ inputs.github-token }}" }
      run: gh run download "${{ inputs.run-id }}" --repo "${{ inputs.repo }}" --name "${{ inputs.name }}" --dir "${{ inputs.path }}"
```

I hope this helps others. I believe that unzip-stream could be completely replaced for most people with this.

Regards
Let me nudge and see why we cannot move this forward
